change: No changes. Primary biceps (Biceps Brachii) and secondary forearms (Wrist Flexors) are correct for a supinated-grip resistance band curl. EMG studies confirm Biceps Brachii as prime mover; Wrist Flexors engage for grip stabilization.

No changes. Primary biceps (Biceps Brachii) is correct. Secondary forearms listing both Wrist Extensors and Wrist Flexors is appropriate for the neutral/hammer grip, which activates brachioradialis (mapped to Wrist Extensors) and forearm flexors for grip. Seated position correctly omits Erector Spinae.

No changes. Same muscle logic as seated variant plus Erector Spinae (Lower Back) as secondary stabilizer for upright posture during standing position — confirmed appropriate by ACE and MuscleAndStrength references.

No changes. Abs (both heads) as primary is correct for this supine knee-pull crunch pattern. Obliques (both) as secondary anti-rotation stabilizer is correct. Quads (Rectus Femoris) as secondary hip flexor contributor is appropriate. Hip flexor (iliopsoas) is not directly mappable to an allowed latin term; Rectus Femoris under Quads is the closest valid representation.

No changes. Abs (both heads) and Abductor (hip flexors/tensor fasciae latae) as co-primary is supported — lying leg raises strongly engage hip flexors alongside rectus abdominis. Secondary Quads (Rectus Femoris for knee extension stabilization), obliques (anti-rotation), and Lower Back (Erector Spinae for spinal stabilization) are all biomechanically justified.
